findings.reason: ComposeEndpoints.cs:51 catches only InvalidOperationException and returns NotFound. Program.cs has no UseExceptionHandler or ProblemDetails (grep finds none), so SmtpCommandException, socket and auth errors become 500s. MailKit's ServiceNotAuthenticatedException derives from InvalidOperationException, so it is reported as a missing mailbox. MailboxEndpoints.cs:73 stores a null SMTP password when none is given, which makes that path reachable. SendMailFailed appears only in the resx files.
findings.claim: Send endpoint maps every InvalidOperationException to 404 MailboxNotFound and lets other SMTP/IMAP/crypto failures escape as 500s; SendMailFailed is never used.
findings.evidence: SendMailAsync wraps the service call in `try { ... } catch (InvalidOperationException) { return Results.NotFound(new { message = localizer["MailboxNotFound"].Value }); }`. Program.cs has no UseExceptionHandler or ProblemDetails. A grep finds SendMailFailed only in the four ApiMessages*.resx files, never in code. Traced case: MailSendingService.SendViaSmtpAsync skips AUTH when `SmtpEncryptedPassword` is empty, which MailboxEndpoints.CreateMailboxAsync stores as null when no password is given. The server then answers 530 and MailKit throws ServiceNotAuthenticatedException, a subclass of InvalidOperationException, so the user gets 404 MailboxNotFound. SmtpCommandException, AuthenticationException, SocketException and CryptographicException from `protector.Unprotect` are not caught at all and become 500s.

findings.reason: The diff uses `client.GetFolder(SpecialFolder.Sent) ?? ...` inside a catch-all that only logs a warning. On servers with neither SPECIAL-USE nor XLIST, MailKit's GetFolder(SpecialFolder) throws NotSupportedException rather than returning null, so the `??` fallback is skipped and the send still returns success. The fallback also matches only the name "Sent".
findings.claim: Sent-folder name fallback never runs on servers without SPECIAL-USE/XLIST because GetFolder(SpecialFolder) throws, and the sent copy is silently dropped.
findings.evidence: `var sent = client.GetFolder(SpecialFolder.Sent) ?? (await client.GetFoldersAsync(client.PersonalNamespaces[0], ...)).FirstOrDefault(f => f.Name.Equals("Sent", ...))`. MailKit's ImapClient.GetFolder(SpecialFolder) throws NotSupportedException when the server advertises neither SPECIAL-USE nor XLIST; it does not return null. That exception skips the `??` branch and lands in `catch (Exception ex) { logger.LogWarning(...) }`, and SendMailAsync still returns the message ID. The name match also accepts only "Sent", so common names such as "Sent Items" and "Sent Messages" are missed. The repo's dev IMAP server is GreenMail (docs/phases/phase-3-mail/05-greenmail-dev-server.md).

findings.reason: quill-interop.js getHtml returns `this._instance.root.innerHTML`, with Quill 2.0.3 loaded. Quill 2 renders bullets as `<ol><li data-list="bullet">` and depends on its own CSS. HtmlSanitizer's defaults strip data-* attributes, so the bullet marker is lost. getSemanticHTML is not used.
findings.claim: getHtml returns Quill's internal root.innerHTML instead of semantic HTML, so bullet lists and indents can reach recipients and Turndown as numbered lists or plain divs.
findings.evidence: `getHtml: function () { return this._instance.root.innerHTML; }` with Quill 2.0.3 loaded (index.html:56), and the toolbar offers `{ 'list': 'bullet' }` and indent and code-block buttons. Quill 2 renders every list as `<ol>` with `<li data-list="bullet">` and relies on its own CSS and classes (ql-indent-N, ql-code-block). Its getSemanticHTML() exists to produce portable `<ul>`/`<ol>` markup. Server-side, OutgoingHtmlSanitizer uses HtmlSanitizer defaults, which strip data-* attributes, and the recipient's mail client has no Quill CSS, so a bullet list is shown numbered. The same markup goes to Turndown when switching to Markdown (`markedInterop.toMarkdown(html)`), so bullets become `1.` items there too.
